name: Filtered feedback-delay resonator: bipolar feedback, swappable loop filter type, dry mute, insert on existing sounds
goal: Turn a single filtered feedback delay into a playable 'renegade' Karplus-Strong voice and a resonator insert: impulse (noise burst or fast sine sweep, no loop) into a ~1–24 ms delay with feedback limited to ±99% (negative = hollow/odd-harmonic, positive = brighter), macro the in-loop filter type (LP/HP/BP/notch, with resonance on BP/notch) and cutoff as timbre controls, mute the dry click, map keys inversely onto delay time (long = low), then reuse the same delay as a metallic-body resonator on basses/pads — the delta beyond our key-tracked KS pluck skill is bipolar feedback polarity, loop-filter-type morphing, dry-mute and the resonator-insert use.

source.title: KARPLUS-STRONG synthesis in Renoise and the •REZONATOR•

prerequisites: Delay with feedback and an in-loop filter (or DelayNode + BiquadFilter in a feedback loop / AudioWorklet)
An impulse source: short noise burst or fast high-to-low sine sweep

inputs.name: impulse
inputs.description: Very short full-spectrum impulse (noise burst or sine sweep), not looped

inputs.name: source_sound
inputs.description: Existing bass/pad to resonate when used as an insert

outputs.name: ks_tone
outputs.description: Pitched/atonal string-like or metallic resonant tone

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Feedback is capped at ±99% to avoid runaway self-oscillation.
Delay-line pitch changes glide (rubber-band portamento) — inherent, use it musically.
Web Audio: a feedback DelayNode cannot go below one render quantum (128 samples, ~2.7 ms @48k) — use an AudioWorklet delay for high pitches (implementation note, not transcript content).
Negative-feedback = polarity-inverted loop; transcript describes it as more square-like vs saw-like for positive.

steps.action: Prepare a full-frequency impulse: a short white-noise burst or a fast sine sweep from very high to low frequency. Set it to one-shot (no loop) so it is only a click.
Insert a delay with feedback and an in-loop filter. Start around 24 ms delay, feedback 50%, effect amount full, filter low-pass fully open.
steps.expect: Pitched ringing tone appears from the click

steps.action: Make performance macros: (1) L+R feedback with range −99…+99 (centre = almost no repeats; negative = hollow square-like character; positive = saw-like), (2) delay time L+R capped at ~24 ms as 'pitch', (3) filter cutoff.
steps.expect: Feedback near ±99 gives long tails without running away; cutoff changes timbre/pitch character

steps.action: For keyboard pitch: map key tracking onto delay time inversely — lowest key → ~24 ms (slow cycle = low pitch), highest key → ~1 ms.
steps.expect: Higher keys give higher pitch, with a slight glide between notes

steps.action: Add a macro for filter type (LP/HP/BP/notch) and automate/record it. With bandpass or notch, raise resonance somewhat — they sound better slightly resonant.
steps.expect: Distinct resonant timbres per filter type; notch visible on a spectrogram

steps.action: Mute the dry signal so the impulse click disappears and only the resonance remains; optionally add drive in the loop (can scream) and a following delay.
steps.expect: Clean resonant tone without the leading click; harmonics grow with drive

steps.action: Try different impulse sources (sine, saw, more or less pitched) — the impulse strongly changes the timbre.
steps.expect: Timbral variety from the same delay setting

steps.action: Resonator insert: put the same delay (wrapped in a macro rack) on an existing bass or pad; tune delay/filter to taste (check filter isn't left on high-pass), keep it subtle or brighter/distorted.
steps.expect: Source gains a metallic-chamber body, depth and presence — reverb-like but resonant

steps.action: Resample interesting results for further processing.

verification: With dry muted, a single impulse yields a pitched/resonant tail and no click.
Flipping feedback sign audibly changes the harmonic character (hollower when negative).
Changing delay time shifts pitch; key mapping is inverted (long delay = low).
Resonator insert on a bass adds audible metallic body vs bypass.
